children.text: astināstivyatikrāntā buddhir yeṣāṃ nirāśrayā |
children.translated_text: Those whose intellect has transcended existence and non-existence, being without support —

children.text: gambhīras tair nirālambaḥ pratyayārtho vibhāvyate || NagYsk_01
children.translated_text: by them the profound, groundless meaning of dependent origination (<s>pratyayārtha</s>) is realized.

children.text: saṃsāraṃ caiva nirvāṇaṃ manyante 'tattvadarśinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who do not see reality (<s>atattvadarśins</s>) conceive of both <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: na saṃsāraṃ na nirvāṇaṃ manyante tattvadarśinaḥ || NagYsk_05
children.translated_text: those who see reality (<s>tattvadarśins</s>) conceive of neither <s>saṃsāra</s> nor <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ ca bhavaś caiva dvayam etan na vidyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and becoming (<s>bhava</s>) — this duality does not exist;

children.text: parajñānaṃ bhavasyaiva nirvāṇam iti kathyate || NagYsk_06
children.translated_text: the thorough knowledge of becoming itself is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: tat tat prāpya yad utpannaṃ notpannaṃ tat svabhāvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever arises having obtained such-and-such [conditions], that has not arisen by its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>);

children.text: svabhāvena yan notpannam utpannaṃ nāma tat katham || NagYsk_19
children.translated_text: that which has not arisen by its own nature — how can it be called 'arisen'?

children.text: sarvam astīti vaktavyam ādau tattvagaveṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: At first, one who investigates reality should say 'everything exists';

children.text: paścād avagatārthasya niḥsaṅgasya viviktatā || NagYsk_30
children.translated_text: afterward, for one who has understood the meaning, who is free from attachment — [there is] detachment.

children.text: mamety aham iti proktaṃ yathā kāryavaśāj jinaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as 'mine' and 'I' were spoken by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) according to practical necessity,

children.text: tathā kāryavaśāt proktāḥ skandhāyatanadhātavaḥ || NagYsk_33
children.translated_text: so too the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements) were spoken according to practical necessity.

children.text: mahābhūtādi vijñāne proktaṃ samavarudhyate |
children.translated_text: The great elements and so forth are said to be subsumed in consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>);

children.text: tajjñāne vagamaṃ yāti nanu mithyā vikalpitam || NagYsk_34
children.translated_text: when that knowledge ceases, are they not falsely constructed?

children.text: hetutaḥ saṃbhavo yasya sthitir na pratyayair vinā |
children.translated_text: That whose arising depends on causes, whose persistence is not without conditions,

children.text: vigamaḥ pratyayābhāvāt so 'stīty avagataḥ katham || NagYsk_39
children.translated_text: whose cessation is from the absence of conditions — how is that understood as 'existing'?

children.text: rāgadveṣodbhavas tīvraduṣṭadṛṣṭiparigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Born from attachment and aversion, the embrace of intensely corrupt views,

children.text: vivādās tatsamutthāś ca bhāvābhyupagame sati || NagYsk_46
children.translated_text: and the disputes that arise from them — [all occur] when there is acceptance of [inherent] existence.

children.text: sa hetuḥ sarvadṛṣṭīnāṃ kleśotpattir na taṃ vinā |
children.translated_text: That [acceptance of existence] is the cause of all [wrong] views; without it, <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) do not arise;

children.text: tasmāt tasmin parijñāte dṛṣṭikleśaparikṣayaḥ || NagYsk_47
children.translated_text: therefore, when it is thoroughly known, views and afflictions are completely exhausted.

children.text: parijñā tasya keneti pratītyotpādadarśanāt |
children.translated_text: How is that thoroughly known? — Through seeing dependent origination (<s>pratītyotpāda</s>);

children.text: pratītya jātaṃ cājātam āha tattvavidāṃ varaḥ || NagYsk_48
children.translated_text: the best among those who know reality declared that what is dependently arisen is unborn.

children.text: bālāḥ sajjanti rūpeṣu vairāgyaṃ yānti madhyamāḥ |
children.translated_text: Fools are attached to forms; the mediocre develop dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>);

children.text: svabhāvajñā vimucyante rūpasyottamabuddhayaḥ || NagYsk_55
children.translated_text: those of supreme wisdom, who know the essential nature [of forms], are liberated.
